title: Added a built-in XLSX engine, so `importFile: true` and `exportFile: true` read and write `.xlsx` files without ExcelJS; `engines: { xlsx: ExcelJS }` keeps working. With no engine configured, the "To Excel" context menu item is shown, `supportsExportFormat('xlsx')` and `supportsImportFormat('xlsx')` return `true`, and an XLSX export or import succeeds; `engines: { xlsx: null }` and a per-call `engine: null` mean "no engine" and use the built-in one. A non-finite number (`NaN`, `Infinity`) now exports as text. Fixed merged-cell meta left behind and `customBorders` throwing after a `loadData`/`updateData` that shrank the grid, `clearBorders()` leaving a border's meta (and its export) behind while rows were sorted or filtered, an XLSX export freezing extra columns or rows when some were hidden, an empty checkbox exporting as `FALSE`, a cleared `numeric` cell exporting as `0`, an XLSX export downloading `[object Promise]` under Zone.js (Angular), the Formulas plugin losing a validated write when `updateSettings()` or a sheet switch ran in the same task, and `removeCellMeta()` throwing for an index past the grid's range (it now removes the key at that physical index, like `setCellMeta()`).
